heroes.name: Crusader
heroes.summary: A durable frontline fighter who can strike, stun, protect himself, and provide small health and stress recovery.

overview.positions: Ranks 1 and 2 keep Smite and Stunning Blow available. Rank 3 is a situational alternative for Holy Lance, which advances the Crusader when used.
strengths: Durable frontline fighter with strong melee damage.
Can stun front enemies and deal bonus damage to Unholy foes.
Offers small party health, stress, and torch recovery.
weaknesses: Very low base Speed means many enemies and allies may act first.
Most direct attacks are limited to the front; Holy Lance is needed to reach back ranks.
overview.beginnerAdvice: Start in rank 1 or 2 and use Smite or Stunning Blow against a front threat. If the party is shuffled, Holy Lance can reach deeper enemies and move him forward.

bosses.name: Necromancer
bosses.summary: An Unholy/Eldritch Ruins boss who retreats as he summons skeletons, steadily changing the enemy formation.

mechanics.text: The Necromancer starts in the front rank. Attacking moves him back one rank and normally summons a skeleton; a stun or three existing skeletons prevents that summon.
Skeleton minions summoned by the Necromancer are linked to him and are removed when he is defeated.
At higher difficulties, summoned Bone Soldiers can begin with Stealth; higher tiers can also summon Bone Defenders that Guard him.

attacks.text: The Flesh Is Willing attacks the front ranks while summoning a skeleton.
The Clawing Dead pressures the rear ranks while summoning a skeleton.
Six Feet Under targets the party with stress pressure and summons a skeleton.

tacticalConsiderations.text: Editorial: plan to reach the rear ranks as he retreats; the source guide describes back-rank pressure as a practical way to shorten the fight.
Editorial: his listed Bleed and Blight resistance is lower than his Stun resistance, but this does not account for other Ruins enemies or party constraints.

bosses.name: Swine Prince
bosses.summary: A large Beast boss supported by Wilbur, whose marks set up the Prince’s strongest attacks.

mechanics.text: The Swine Prince occupies enemy ranks 1–3; Wilbur stands in rank 4.
Wilbur marks one or two heroes, and the Prince can answer those marks with focused attacks. With no marks, the Prince uses Wild Flailing instead.
Damaging Wilbur while the Prince is alive triggers Enraged Destruction against the whole party. Defeating Wilbur first makes the Prince use that attack each round.

attacks.text: End This One and End These Two are Wilbur’s mark skills.
Obliterate Body and Obliterate Masses target marked heroes.
Enraged Destruction is the response to damaging Wilbur while the Prince remains alive.
Bit ’o Squeal can stun the party at higher quest levels.

tacticalConsiderations.text: Editorial: concentrate attacks on the Swine Prince and avoid damaging Wilbur while the Prince is still alive; this follows the source guide’s warning about Enraged Destruction.
Editorial: be cautious with Riposte because an automatic counter can hit Wilbur and trigger the same retaliation.

Editorial: at Champion, favor Accuracy on the heroes expected to deal damage and Stun resistance on support heroes who need to act through Wilbur’s added Stun pressure. The Prince has higher health and Bleed/Blight resistance at higher tiers, so neither damage-over-time nor Stun should be treated as guaranteed.

counterTeams.name: Beginner · remove marks and focus the Prince
counterTeams.purpose: A base-game answer to Wilbur’s setup: Arbalest clears Mark and Stun while Houndmaster and Hellion attack the Swine Prince.
counterTeams.difficultyRecommendations: Apprentice, Veteran and Champion; Wilbur gains an additional Stun action at higher tiers, so Rallying Flare becomes especially valuable.

members.role: Mark removal, recovery and ranged damage
members.tacticalPriority: Read Wilbur’s marks each round. Use Rallying Flare to clear party Marks and Stun; otherwise use Sniper Shot on the Prince, never Wilbur.
members.budgetPriorities: Stun resistance helps preserve her chance to act on Rallying Flare; then prioritize Accuracy for Sniper Shot and damage for a faster kill.
members.equipmentRationale: Damage Stone favors stronger direct shots and Reckless Charm adds Accuracy; both trade away Dodge, so this is an aggressive common-rarity pairing rather than a guaranteed early-game drop.

members.role: Damage reduction, mark support and emergency heal
members.tacticalPriority: Weakening Curse reduces the Prince’s damage; Vulnerability Hex or direct attacks can contribute when the danger is controlled.
members.budgetPriorities: Prioritize Stun resistance so the damage-reduction/debuff turn remains available, then Accuracy for offensive skills; healing support has no guaranteed result.
members.equipmentRationale: Reckless Charm supports the accuracy of offensive/debuff actions; Damage Stone only helps direct damage, not Wyrd Reconstruction. Prioritize the stated Stun-resistance fallback if available.

members.role: Beast damage, mark payoff and Guard

members.budgetPriorities: Prioritize Stun resistance and Accuracy; damage supports Hound’s Rush, while guarding a marked ally is the defensive fallback.
members.equipmentRationale: Damage Stone supports direct attacks and Reckless Charm supports accuracy; both reduce Dodge, so use them only if the lower evasion is acceptable for this hero.

members.tacticalPriority: Spend attacks on the Prince’s ranks 1–3. Keep all targeting away from Wilbur until the Prince is defeated.
members.budgetPriorities: Prioritize Accuracy and damage for focused attacks; Stun resistance helps prevent losing a turn while Wilbur is applying pressure.
members.equipmentRationale: Damage Stone supports direct attacks and Reckless Charm supports accuracy; both reduce Dodge, so use them only if the lower evasion is acceptable for this hero.

counterTeams.openingStrategy: Target the Swine Prince in enemy ranks 1–3. Use Target Whistle to mark the Prince for Houndmaster’s Hound’s Rush; the Arbalest can use Sniper Shot or Rallying Flare depending on whether Wilbur has marked or stunned the party.
counterTeams.alternatives: Musketeer can fill the Arbalest’s Mark/Stun removal role with Skeet Shot, but this is a DLC class. Recheck skills and rank positions before substituting; the listed team is base-game.

battlePlan.beforeEntering: Equip Rallying Flare on the Arbalest and confirm the team’s ranks. The encounter is in the Warrens. This team data does not specify provision quantities.
battlePlan.openingTurns: Target the Swine Prince in enemy ranks 1–3. Use Target Whistle to mark the Prince for Houndmaster’s Hound’s Rush; the Arbalest can use Sniper Shot or Rallying Flare depending on whether Wilbur has marked or stunned the party.
battlePlan.bossMechanic: Wilbur marks one or two heroes for the Prince’s heavy attacks. Rallying Flare clears Mark and Stun from the other three heroes; it does not clear the Arbalest herself. If the Arbalest is stunned or marked, use Guard Dog, healing, or damage reduction while preserving the focus fire.
battlePlan.guardAndControl: Do not damage Wilbur while the Prince lives. Any damaging hit on Wilbur triggers Enraged Destruction, and killing Wilbur makes the Prince use it repeatedly. Avoid Riposte that could hit Wilbur. This team relies on Rallying Flare, Guard Dog and Weakening Curse rather than a Wilbur kill.
battlePlan.recoveryAndLimits: Arbalest Bandage heals one ally; Occultist’s Wyrd Reconstruction is an emergency heal with variable results. The team has no dependable party heal, so clearing Mark/Stun and reducing incoming damage should take priority over waiting for recovery.
detailedNotes: On Veteran and Champion, Wilbur uses Bit o’ Squeal at the start of each round and can Stun the party. Rallying Flare can clear that Stun along with Marks when the Arbalest gets a turn.
After the Prince dies, Wilbur stops marking and uses Squeal. The quest objective is complete when the Prince is defeated; do not risk a weakened party during unnecessary cleanup.

battlePlan.openingTurns: The Prince occupies enemy ranks 1–3. Attack it directly. If Wilbur marks someone, clear the mark and any Stun on allies with Rallying Flare, or guard/heal the target if the Arbalest cannot act.

counterTeams.openingStrategy: If turn order allows, use Battle Ballad and Mark for Death before Bounty Hunter attacks; otherwise deal direct damage and set up the mark on a later turn. Aim all damaging effects at the Prince and keep Rallying Flare for danger.

battlePlan.recoveryAndLimits: There is no dedicated healer. Arbalest Bandage heals one ally and Hellion can use Adrenaline Rush on herself; neither replaces party healing. Retreat from a deteriorating expedition rather than treating the fast-kill plan as guaranteed.

counterTeams.openingStrategy: Focus on the Prince from the first action. Keep Rallying Flare ready; use Defender for a marked hero if Flare cannot resolve the danger. Flagellant’s Suffer is a backup clear that transfers the Mark to himself.

battlePlan.beforeEntering: This team requires the Crimson Court DLC and Flagellant. Check the party order: Arbalest 4, Man-at-Arms 3, Flagellant 2, Leper 1. Named trinket acquisition may be unknown.

commonMistakes.name: Damage Wilbur before the Prince is dead
commonMistakes.text: Any damaging hit on Wilbur triggers Enraged Destruction against the whole party. Killing Wilbur first makes the Prince repeat it each round.

commonMistakes.name: Let an automatic Riposte hit Wilbur
commonMistakes.text: Do not activate Riposte while Wilbur is alive unless you can guarantee it will not target him; an automatic damaging counter can trigger the same retaliation.

commonMistakes.name: Assume Rallying Flare clears the Arbalest herself
commonMistakes.text: Rallying Flare clears Mark and Stun from the other party members, not the Arbalest. Keep her protected and use healing or Guard if she is disabled.

commonMistakes.name: Build the plan around stunning the Prince
commonMistakes.text: The Prince’s Stun resistance rises with campaign tier and reaches immunity in the recorded variants. Treat Stun as optional control for Wilbur, not the core answer to the Prince.

commonMistakes.name: Keep fighting after the Prince is defeated
commonMistakes.text: The boss quest objective completes when the Prince dies. Wilbur is not required for the objective; decide whether cleanup is safe before spending turns on him.

bosses.name: Hag
bosses.summary: A Human boss positioned behind a cauldron that captures a party member and forces the rest to adapt.

mechanics.text: The Hag occupies ranks 3–4; the cauldron occupies ranks 1–2. Neither can be moved.
Into the Pot! captures one hero. The captive cannot act and takes damage as turns pass; damaging the filled pot can release them, after which the pot can be used again.
When the captive reaches Death’s Door, the pot releases them. Defeating the Hag also releases the captive and ends the encounter.
The Hag has multiple actions per round and uses party attacks and stress effects while a hero is trapped.

attacks.text: Into the Pot! selects a hero and places them in the cauldron.
Meat Tenderizer attacks the heroes outside the pot.
Season to Perfection applies a damage and accuracy debuff; Taste the Stew is used in relation to a trapped hero.

tacticalConsiderations.text: Editorial: bring attacks that can reach ranks 3–4 and expect the active party formation to shift when someone is captured.
Editorial: the source recommends balancing damage to the Hag with timely recovery for a hero released at critical health; the cauldron’s occupant cannot use skills while trapped.

members.role: Rank-flexible damage, mark support and Guard
members.tacticalPriority: Use Hound’s Rush against the Hag; reserve Guard Dog for a vulnerable ally if the pot and repeated Hag actions create danger.
members.budgetPriorities: Prioritize Stun resistance and Accuracy; damage supports Hound’s Rush, while guarding a marked ally is the defensive fallback.
members.equipmentRationale: The listed pairing supports rank-flexible damage, mark support and guard; compare the canonical effects and requirements below before choosing alternatives.

members.role: Flexible direct attacks into the rear ranks
members.tacticalPriority: Pistol Shot and Tracking Shot can reach the Hag from this starting position; reassess after the party shifts.
members.budgetPriorities: Prioritize Accuracy and damage; avoid Riposte skills that can retaliate against Wilbur.
members.equipmentRationale: The listed pairing supports flexible direct attacks into the rear ranks; compare the canonical effects and requirements below before choosing alternatives.

members.role: Front-line damage with Iron Swan reach
members.tacticalPriority: Iron Swan is the selected rank 4 attack from the front; do not spend the turn attacking the empty cauldron.
members.budgetPriorities: Prioritize Accuracy and damage for focused attacks; Stun resistance helps prevent losing a turn while Wilbur is applying pressure.
members.equipmentRationale: The listed pairing supports front-line damage with iron swan reach; compare the canonical effects and requirements below before choosing alternatives.

counterTeams.openingStrategy: Attack the Hag in enemy ranks 3–4 immediately. The Occultist and Houndmaster can mark her for follow-up attacks; use Weakening Curse when reducing incoming pressure is more useful than another attack.
counterTeams.alternatives: No drop-in replacements are recorded as mechanically equivalent. If substituting a hero, verify that the replacement can attack enemy rank 3 or 4 from the assigned position and after likely formation shifts.

battlePlan.beforeEntering: Equip the listed skills and check each hero is in ranks 4→1. The Hag is encountered in the Weald. No fixed provision quantities are recorded for this composition.
battlePlan.openingTurns: Attack the Hag in enemy ranks 3–4 immediately. The Occultist and Houndmaster can mark her for follow-up attacks; use Weakening Curse when reducing incoming pressure is more useful than another attack.
battlePlan.bossMechanic: The cauldron occupies enemy ranks 1–2 and the Hag stays in 3–4. Into the Pot removes one hero from the fight; continue with the other three and focus the Hag. Attack the filled cauldron only when freeing its occupant is worth losing an attack on the boss.
battlePlan.guardAndControl: The Hag and cauldron cannot be moved. Do not plan around pulls or stuns; this team instead keeps multiple attacks that reach the Hag’s fixed back ranks.
battlePlan.recoveryAndLimits: Wyrd Reconstruction is the Occultist’s uncertain emergency heal; Houndmaster can Guard an ally. If the captured hero is your main damage source, consider freeing them; otherwise keep damaging the Hag. A captured hero cannot retreat with the party.
detailedNotes: The Hag acts more than once per round, so the trapped hero loses health during both party and boss actions. If released at Death’s Door, heal promptly because another party-wide hit may follow.

The cauldron cannot be damaged while empty. The Hag is resistant to Stun and Blight and more vulnerable to Bleed; this lineup primarily uses direct attacks, so it does not depend on a status effect landing.

bosses.name: Siren
bosses.summary: An Eldritch boss with two actions per round who can charm an equipped hero and turn that hero against the party.

mechanics.text: The Siren takes two turns per round.
Song of Desire can charm one hero. The controlled hero can use equipped combat skills, then returns to the party in rank 4 after the charm ends.
A charmed hero is placed in a rank adjacent to the Siren and takes stress while controlled; the charm can also target heroes in Stealth.
The Siren can summon Pelagic enemies and use attacks that apply party-wide Bleed or stress.

attacks.text: Song of Desire is the hero-control ability.
Pressure Crash targets the party with stress damage.
Devour applies Bleed; High Tide can summon an aquatic reinforcement.

tacticalConsiderations.text: Editorial: prepare for the party to operate with three heroes while one is charmed, and expect the returning hero to re-enter at the back.
Editorial: use area attacks carefully while a controlled party member is among the enemies; keep movement options available to restore formation.

counterTeams.name: Balanced · charm bait and guarded pressure
counterTeams.purpose: A base-game team that uses the Antiquarian as a low-threat likely charm target while Houndmaster and Man-at-Arms provide selectable Guard support.
counterTeams.difficultyRecommendations: Apprentice, Veteran and Champion; charm and action-economy tactics apply across variants, but tier performance is not tested.

members.role: Low-threat support and likely charm bait
members.tacticalPriority: The Antiquarian is a likely charm target because of low Debuff resistance, not a guaranteed one. Keep her equipped actions low-threat and avoid using dangerous damage into allies if she is controlled.
members.budgetPriorities: Prioritize Stun resistance and survivability; her role is utility, so do not spend the full equipment plan on damage.
members.equipmentRationale: The listed pairing supports low-threat support and likely charm bait; compare the canonical effects and requirements below before choosing alternatives.

members.role: Direct back-rank pressure and party recovery
members.tacticalPriority: Use Sniper Shot to keep direct pressure on the Siren. Rallying Flare can clear party Mark and Stun; Battlefield Bandage provides one-target recovery.
members.budgetPriorities: Stun resistance helps preserve her chance to act on Rallying Flare; then prioritize Accuracy for Sniper Shot and damage for a faster kill.
members.equipmentRationale: The listed pairing supports direct back-rank pressure and party recovery; compare the canonical effects and requirements below before choosing alternatives.

members.tacticalPriority: Guard Dog can protect one chosen hero from charm. If the Houndmaster is charmed, he may use that skill on the Siren, so maintain control and avoid assuming Guard is permanent.
members.budgetPriorities: Prioritize Stun resistance and Accuracy; damage supports Hound’s Rush, while guarding a marked ally is the defensive fallback.
members.equipmentRationale: The listed pairing supports single-target damage and flexible guard; compare the canonical effects and requirements below before choosing alternatives.

members.role: Front-line pressure and a second Guard option
members.tacticalPriority: Use Defender to guard a chosen ally. Rampart only reaches enemy ranks 1–2 from this position, so use it on a Pelagic Guardian there if it is guarding the Siren.
members.budgetPriorities: Prioritize Stun resistance and survivability so Defender remains available; Accuracy matters less when using Guard and party buffs.
members.equipmentRationale: The listed pairing supports front-line pressure and a second guard option; compare the canonical effects and requirements below before choosing alternatives.

counterTeams.openingStrategy: Use direct attacks on the Siren rather than spending repeated turns marking her; she acts twice per round, so debuffs and marks need frequent upkeep. Keep Houndmaster’s and Man-at-Arms’s Guard actions available for a hero you need to protect.
counterTeams.alternatives: No fully verified drop-in replacement is recorded. If replacing a Guard hero, retain another verified Guard option and check the new hero’s skills after the Siren returns a charmed hero to rank 4.

battlePlan.beforeEntering: Equip the listed skills and confirm the rank order. Keep Antiquarian’s low Debuff resistance in mind: the Siren often favors the hero with the lowest resistance, but charm can still select someone else.
battlePlan.openingTurns: Use direct attacks on the Siren rather than spending repeated turns marking her; she acts twice per round, so debuffs and marks need frequent upkeep. Keep Houndmaster’s and Man-at-Arms’s Guard actions available for a hero you need to protect.
battlePlan.bossMechanic: Song of Desire can take control of an equipped hero, so plan to play with three. A returning hero is placed in rank 4. Avoid area attacks that could hit a charmed teammate and reassess skill positions after the return.
battlePlan.guardAndControl: Guard Dog and Defender can prevent the selected hero from being charmed. A charmed Guard user can instead Guard the Siren; if that happens, use Man-at-Arms Rampart only when the guarding Pelagic Guardian is in enemy rank 1 or 2.
battlePlan.recoveryAndLimits: Arbalest’s Battlefield Bandage heals one ally and Rallying Flare can clear Stun. The team has no full-party HP heal. The Antiquarian’s low-threat role reduces the cost of a likely charm but does not prevent charm or remove the threat from another hero being selected.
detailedNotes: The Siren takes two turns per round and may summon Pelagic reinforcements. Stuns can interrupt a dangerous summon or a charmed hero, but the exact turn order is not guaranteed.
Do not flee while a hero is charmed. The returned hero goes to rank 4, so check that the Arbalest and Antiquarian can still perform their selected skills from the resulting ranks.

locations.name: Ruins
locations.summary: An ancient stone complex populated by undead and cultists.
specialMechanics: The region roster is primarily Unholy. Bone enemies resist Bleed heavily; Blight is generally more effective against them.

locations.name: Warrens
locations.summary: A corpse-choked tunnel network inhabited by Swinefolk and scavengers.
specialMechanics: Swine enemies commonly combine Human and Beast types. Disease threats and low Bleed resistance are recurring features.

locations.name: Weald
locations.summary: A corrupted woodland where fungal creatures, beasts, and bandits converge.
specialMechanics: Many local enemies resist Blight well and are comparatively vulnerable to Bleed. Fungal enemies can spread Blight and disease.

locations.name: Cove
locations.summary: A flooded coast inhabited by fishfolk and Eldritch creatures.
specialMechanics: Many fishfolk resist Bleed and are more vulnerable to Blight. Several encounters threaten heroes with Bleed and formation disruption.

locations.name: Courtyard
locations.summary: A Crimson Court expedition centered on Bloodsuckers and the Crimson Curse.
specialMechanics: Bloodsuckers resist Blight and are weak to Bleed; after the first Courtyard mission, some appear in the four main regions.

locations.name: Farmstead
locations.summary: A Color of Madness endless expedition through crystalline corruption.
specialMechanics: The region is a Color of Madness endless expedition. Farmstead-only Husk enemies coexist with recurring enemies from elsewhere.

locations.name: Darkest Dungeon
locations.summary: The spoiler-sensitive final region, with unique encounters and quest rules.
specialMechanics: This is the spoiler-sensitive endgame region and contains unique enemies and quest mechanics.

quests.name: Short expeditions
quests.summary: Standard short missions have no camp phase and no firewood provision.

quests.name: Medium expeditions
quests.summary: Standard medium missions include one camp phase.
specialMechanics: One camp phase; firewood is supplied automatically.

quests.name: Long expeditions
quests.summary: Standard long missions include two camp phases.
specialMechanics: Two camp phases; firewood is supplied automatically.

quests.name: Shrieker's Perch
quests.summary: A special encounter that becomes available after losing enough trinkets.
specialMechanics: This is a named special quest tied to the Shrieker encounter.

quests.name: The Crimson Court questline
quests.summary: A staged DLC questline that introduces the Courtyard and Crimson Curse.
specialMechanics: Quest progression and infestation affect access and encounter context.

quests.name: Farmstead expeditions
quests.summary: The Color of Madness adds an endless expedition with waves of enemies and shard rewards.
specialMechanics: The expedition uses wave progression; standard dungeon duration labels do not apply.

quests.name: Darkest Dungeon quests
quests.summary: A sequence of named endgame missions with unique objectives and encounters.

quests.name: Cleanse
quests.summary: Clear the required room battles; corridor fights do not count toward the room objective.

quests.name: Explore
quests.summary: Visit 90% of dungeon rooms. The map can be completed without entering every room.

quests.name: Gather
quests.summary: Collect the quest-marked heirlooms from curios and return to town.

quests.name: Activate
quests.summary: Use the supplied quest item on the designated curio.

quests.name: Boss expedition
quests.summary: Defeat the target boss. Boss missions use medium-length dungeons.
